title: Equations of Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
seo_title: Algebra I Parallel and Perpendicular Lines Worksheets (TEKS A.2E, A.2F)
standard_text: A.2E write the equation of a line that contains a given point and is parallel to a given line; A.2F write the equation of a line that contains a given point and is perpendicular to a given line; A.2G write an equation of a line that is parallel or perpendicular to the x- or y-axis and determine whether the slope of the line is zero or undefined
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.2E, A.2F and A.2G: parallel and perpendicular slopes, equations of parallel and perpendicular lines and lines parallel to the axes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Parallel: same slope. Perpendicular: opposite reciprocal.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Parallel lines have the same slope.
  • Perpendicular lines have slopes that are opposite reciprocals: 2 and −12.
  • Use the new slope and the given point in point-slope form.
  • A line parallel to the x-axis is horizontal: y = b. A line parallel to the y-axis is vertical: x = a.

Examples

Example

Perpendicular to y = 2x + 1 through (4, 3)

slope −1/2

3 = −1/2(4) + b, b = 5

Answer: y = −1/2x + 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Same slope for perpendicular linesFlip the fraction and change the sign.
Forgetting to change the signThe reciprocal of 3 for a perpendicular line is −1/3.
Writing x = a for a horizontal lineHorizontal lines are y = b.

items.q: A line passes through (−5, 1) and (−3, 7). What is the slope of a line perpendicular to it?
items.e: Slope = (7 − 1) ÷ (−3 − (−5)) = 3. Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals: −13.

items.q: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to y = 4x + 4?
items.e: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals: flip 4 and change the sign. −14. Check: 4 × (−14) = −1.

items.e: Slope = (9 − 1) ÷ (−4 − (−6)) = 4. Parallel lines have the same slope: 4.
